claim: SHARPIN regulates immune signaling and contributes to full transcriptional activity and prevention of cell death in response to TNF in vitro.
source: SHARPIN regulates immune signaling and contributes to full transcriptional activity and prevention of cell death in response to TNF in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general background claim about SHARPIN function.

claim: The inactivating mouse Sharpin cpdm mutation causes TNF-dependent multi-organ inflammation, characterized by dermatitis, liver inflammation, splenomegaly, and loss of Peyer's patches.
source: The inactivating mouse Sharpin cpdm mutation causes TNF-dependent multi-organ inflammation, characterized by dermatitis, liver inflammation, splenomegaly, and loss of Peyer's patches.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Tnfr1, but not Tnfr2, deficiency suppresses the Sharpin-deficient phenotype.
source: TNF-dependent cell death has been proposed to cause the inflammatory phenotype and consistent with this we show Tnfr1, but not Tnfr2, deficiency suppresses the phenotype (and it does so more efficiently than Il1r1 loss).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1, where Shpnm/mTnfr1−/− mice show no disease while Shpnm/mTnfr2−/− mice develop disease.

claim: Tnfr1 deficiency suppresses the Sharpin-deficient phenotype more efficiently than Il1r1 loss.
source: TNF-dependent cell death has been proposed to cause the inflammatory phenotype and consistent with this we show Tnfr1, but not Tnfr2, deficiency suppresses the phenotype (and it does so more efficiently than Il1r1 loss).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1 showing that Shpnm/mTnfr1−/− mice have no disease at 35 weeks while Shpnm/mIl1r1−/− mice develop disease by 19-20 weeks.

claim: Reduction in or loss of caspase-8 and BID generally did not suppress inflammation in Sharpin-deficient mice.
source: TNFR1-induced apoptosis can proceed through caspase-8 and BID, but reduction in or loss of these players generally did not suppress inflammation, although Casp8 heterozygosity significantly delayed dermatitis.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6 showing that Bid deletion did not protect against the cpdm phenotype, while Casp8 heterozygosity delayed but did not prevent dermatitis.

claim: Casp8 heterozygosity significantly delayed dermatitis in Sharpin-deficient mice.
source: TNFR1-induced apoptosis can proceed through caspase-8 and BID, but reduction in or loss of these players generally did not suppress inflammation, although Casp8 heterozygosity significantly delayed dermatitis.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6B showing that 12-week-old Shpnm/mCasp8+/− mice had almost no epidermal hyperplasia compared to Shpnm/m mice.

claim: Ripk3 or Mlkl deficiency partially ameliorated the multi-organ phenotype in Sharpin-deficient mice.
source: Ripk3 or Mlkl deficiency partially ameliorated the multi-organ phenotype, and combined Ripk3 deletion and Casp8 heterozygosity almost completely suppressed it, even restoring Peyer's patches.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 7 showing that Shpnm/mRipk3−/− and Shpnm/mMlkl−/− mice had reduced splenomegaly and liver inflammation.

claim: Combined Ripk3 deletion and Casp8 heterozygosity almost completely suppressed the Sharpin-deficient phenotype, even restoring Peyer's patches.
source: Ripk3 or Mlkl deficiency partially ameliorated the multi-organ phenotype, and combined Ripk3 deletion and Casp8 heterozygosity almost completely suppressed it, even restoring Peyer's patches.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 9 showing that Shpnm/mCasp8+/−Ripk3−/− mice had no skin, liver, or spleen pathology at 12 weeks and had Peyer's patches present.

claim: Sharpin, Ripk3 and Casp8 triple deficiency caused perinatal lethality.
source: Unexpectedly, Sharpin, Ripk3 and Casp8 triple deficiency caused perinatal lethality.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 8A showing that no Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− mice were obtained at weaning, with most dying between E17 and 1-2 days after birth.

claim: Chronic proliferative dermatitis mutation (cpdm) mice are deficient in SHARPIN.
source: Chronic proliferative dermatitis mutation (cpdm) mice are deficient in SHARPIN (Sharpincpdm/cpdm: henceforth referred to as Shpnm/m; protein: SHARPIN) and develop dermatitis, multi-organ pathology and an immunological phenotype including disrupted lymphoid architecture, splenomegaly, liver inflammation and a loss of Peyer's patches in the gut (HogenEsch et al., 1993, 1999; Seymour et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Cpdm mice develop dermatitis, multi-organ pathology and an immunological phenotype including disrupted lymphoid architecture, splenomegaly, liver inflammation and a loss of Peyer's patches in the gut.
source: Chronic proliferative dermatitis mutation (cpdm) mice are deficient in SHARPIN (Sharpincpdm/cpdm: henceforth referred to as Shpnm/m; protein: SHARPIN) and develop dermatitis, multi-organ pathology and an immunological phenotype including disrupted lymphoid architecture, splenomegaly, liver inflammation and a loss of Peyer's patches in the gut (HogenEsch et al., 1993, 1999; Seymour et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: SHARPIN is required for normal TNFR1-mediated gene induction.
source: SHARPIN is required for normal tumour necrosis factor (TNF) receptor 1 (TNFR1)-mediated gene induction and prevention of TNF-mediated death of various cells, including epidermal keratinocytes, in vitro (Gerlach et al., 2011; Ikeda et al., 2011; Tokunaga et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: SHARPIN is required for prevention of TNF-mediated death of various cells, including epidermal keratinocytes, in vitro.
source: SHARPIN is required for normal tumour necrosis factor (TNF) receptor 1 (TNFR1)-mediated gene induction and prevention of TNF-mediated death of various cells, including epidermal keratinocytes, in vitro (Gerlach et al., 2011; Ikeda et al., 2011; Tokunaga et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The dermatitis in cpdm mice is characterized by epidermal cell death marked by cleaved caspase-3-, -8- and -9-positive cells.
source: The dermatitis is characterized by epidermal cell death marked by cleaved caspase-3-, -8- and -9-positive cells (Ikeda et al., 2011; Liang and Sundberg, 2011; Potter et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The dermatitis and inflammatory phenotype in cpdm mice were shown to be TNF dependent.
source: Since the dermatitis and inflammatory phenotype were shown to be TNF dependent, and because the only TNF signaling output that was aberrantly increased in the absence of SHARPIN was cell death, we previously proposed TNF/TNFR1-mediated cell death to be causative of the cpdm phenotype (Gerlach et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The only TNF signaling output that was aberrantly increased in the absence of SHARPIN was cell death.
source: Since the dermatitis and inflammatory phenotype were shown to be TNF dependent, and because the only TNF signaling output that was aberrantly increased in the absence of SHARPIN was cell death, we previously proposed TNF/TNFR1-mediated cell death to be causative of the cpdm phenotype (Gerlach et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: TNFR1 signaling typically involves the intracellular recruitment of TRADD, TRAF2, cIAPs, and RIPK1.
source: TNFR1 signaling typically involves the intracellular recruitment of TNFR1-associated death domain protein (TRADD), TNF receptor-associated factor 2 (TRAF2), cellular inhibitor of apoptosis (cIAPs), and receptor interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1) (Silke, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The heterotrimeric linear ubiquitin chain assembly complex (LUBAC) is composed of SHARPIN, HOIL-1, and HOIP.
source: The heterotrimeric linear ubiquitin chain assembly complex (LUBAC) of SHARPIN (also known as SIPL), HOIL-1 (RBCK1/RNF54) and HOIL-1L-interacting protein (HOIP; RNF31) (Gerlach et al., 2011; Ikeda et al., 2011; Tokunaga et al., 2011) is also recruited to the TNFR1 signaling complex.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: LUBAC is recruited to the TNFR1 signaling complex.
source: The heterotrimeric linear ubiquitin chain assembly complex (LUBAC) of SHARPIN (also known as SIPL), HOIL-1 (RBCK1/RNF54) and HOIL-1L-interacting protein (HOIP; RNF31) (Gerlach et al., 2011; Ikeda et al., 2011; Tokunaga et al., 2011) is also recruited to the TNFR1 signaling complex.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: LUBAC assembles a linear ubiquitin scaffold needed for full recruitment of the NEMO/IKKγ-containing IKK complex, which activates pro-survival NF-κB signaling.
source: Here, it assembles a linear ubiquitin scaffold needed for full recruitment of the NF-κB essential modulator (NEMO)/NF-κB kinase subunit gamma (IKKγ)-containing IKK complex, which activates pro-survival NF-κB signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing LUBAC function.

claim: TNFR1-induced JNK and p38 signaling is regulated by LUBAC.
source: TNFR1-induced c-Jun N-terminal protein kinase (JNK) and p38 signaling is also regulated by LUBAC.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing LUBAC function.

claim: SHARPIN deficiency blunts the TNFR1 pro-survival transcriptional signal and sensitizes cells to TNF-induced cell death.
source: SHARPIN deficiency blunts the TNFR1 pro-survival transcriptional signal and sensitizes cells to TNF-induced cell death.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing the consequences of SHARPIN deficiency.

claim: The E3 ligase activity of HOIP catalyzes the addition of linear ubiquitin to target proteins.
source: The E3 ligase activity of HOIP catalyzes the addition of linear ubiquitin to target proteins, and SHARPIN and HOIL-1 are key regulators of the stability and activity of HOIP (Gerlach et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SHARPIN and HOIL-1 are key regulators of the stability and activity of HOIP.
source: The E3 ligase activity of HOIP catalyzes the addition of linear ubiquitin to target proteins, and SHARPIN and HOIL-1 are key regulators of the stability and activity of HOIP (Gerlach et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: LUBAC regulates the transcriptional response from IL-1R, CD40, LTβR, TLR4, and NOD2 receptor signaling complexes.
source: In addition to TNFR1, LUBAC has also been shown to regulate the transcriptional response from the interleukin-1 receptor (IL-1R), CD40, lymphotoxin beta receptor (LTβR), toll-like-receptor 4 (TLR4), and nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-containing protein 2 (NOD2) receptor signaling complexes (Schmukle and Walczak, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Deletion of Il1rap almost completely prevents the development of cpdm dermatitis.
source: Deletion of Il1rap, needed for IL-1 signaling, has been reported to almost completely prevent the development of cpdm dermatitis (Liang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: IL-1R signaling is a significant driver of disease in cpdm mice.
source: This suggests that IL-1R signaling is a significant driver of disease, but the effect of Il1rap deficiency on the rest of the Shpnm/m phenotype was not reported.
evidence: This is inferred from the reported effect of Il1rap deletion on cpdm dermatitis.

claim: Cpdm mice have prominent eosinophil infiltration into the skin.
source: Cpdm mice have prominent eosinophil infiltration into the skin; however, deletion of Il5, which dramatically reduces the number of cutaneous and circulating eosinophils, fails to ameliorate disease (Renninger et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Deletion of Il5 fails to ameliorate disease in cpdm mice despite dramatically reducing the number of cutaneous and circulating eosinophils.
source: Cpdm mice have prominent eosinophil infiltration into the skin; however, deletion of Il5, which dramatically reduces the number of cutaneous and circulating eosinophils, fails to ameliorate disease (Renninger et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Shpnm/mRag1−/− mice lacking functional lymphocytes develop dermatitis, indicating that T and B cells are not required for the skin phenotype.
source: Shpnm/mRag1−/− mice lacking functional lymphocytes develop dermatitis, indicating that T and B cell cells are not required for the skin phenotype (Potter et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Hematopoietic cell transfer with bone marrow and spleen cells from cpdm mice to syngeneic wild-type C57BL/Ka mice failed to transfer disease in mice 2 months post reconstitution.
source: Furthermore, hematopoietic cell transfer with bone marrow and spleen cells from cpdm mice to syngeneic wild-type C57BL/Ka mice failed to transfer disease in mice 2 months post reconstitution.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: Cpdm skin transplanted onto nude mice retained the donor dermatitis phenotype 3 months post transplant.
source: Finally, cpdm skin transplanted onto nude mice retained the donor dermatitis phenotype 3 months post transplant, while syngeneic healthy skin transplanted onto cpdm mice did not acquire the disease over the same time (HogenEsch et al., 1993; Gijbels et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Syngeneic healthy skin transplanted onto cpdm mice did not acquire the disease over 3 months.
source: Finally, cpdm skin transplanted onto nude mice retained the donor dermatitis phenotype 3 months post transplant, while syngeneic healthy skin transplanted onto cpdm mice did not acquire the disease over the same time (HogenEsch et al., 1993; Gijbels et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: A skin-intrinsic defect in cpdm mice drives the inflammatory disease.
source: Together these studies indicate that a skin-intrinsic defect in cpdm mice drives the inflammatory disease, however they do not rule out a role for the hematopoietic system in amplifying it.
evidence: This is inferred from the transplantation and reconstitution studies cited.

claim: Impaired pro-survival TNFR1 signaling can induce both caspase-8-dependent apoptotic and RIPK3- and MLKL-dependent necroptotic cell death via a cytosolic death platform.
source: Impaired pro-survival TNFR1 signaling can induce both caspase-8-dependent apoptotic and RIPK3- and mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL)-dependent necroptotic cell death via a cytosolic death platform (Micheau and Tschopp, 2003; He et al., 2009; Sun et al., 2012; Zhao et al., 2012; Murphy et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Necroptosis involves the release of cellular contents including potential DAMPs such as mitochondrial DNA, HMGB1, IL-33, and IL-1α.
source: Necroptosis involves the release of cellular contents including potential damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) such as mitochondrial DNA, high mobility group box 1 protein (HMGB1), IL-33, and IL-1α (Kaczmarek et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Apoptosis is considered to be immunologically silent, although this is context dependent.
source: By contrast, apoptosis is considered to be immunologically silent, although this is clearly context dependent because excessive apoptosis resulting from conditional epidermal deletion of the caspase inhibitor cFLIP can cause severe skin inflammation (Panayotova-Dimitrova et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Excessive apoptosis resulting from conditional epidermal deletion of cFLIP can cause severe skin inflammation.
source: By contrast, apoptosis is considered to be immunologically silent, although this is clearly context dependent because excessive apoptosis resulting from conditional epidermal deletion of the caspase inhibitor cFLIP can cause severe skin inflammation (Panayotova-Dimitrova et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Caspase-8 can cleave both RIPK1 and RIPK3 and is needed to keep the necroptotic pathway in check.
source: Caspase-8 can cleave both RIPK1 and RIPK3 and is needed to keep the necroptotic pathway in check (Vandenabeele et al., 2010; Kaiser et al., 2011; Oberst et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Regulation of necroptotic signaling is crucial for skin homeostasis.
source: Regulation of necroptotic signaling is crucial for skin homeostasis because deletion of either caspase-8, the caspase-8 adaptor protein FADD (Fas-associated protein with death domain), or RIPK1, leads to RIPK3- and MLKL-dependent epidermal hyperplasia and inflammation (Kovalenko et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2009; Bonnet et al., 2011; Kaiser et al., 2011; Oberst et al., 2011; Dannappel et al., 2014; Dillon et al., 2014; Rickard et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Deletion of caspase-8, FADD, or RIPK1 leads to RIPK3- and MLKL-dependent epidermal hyperplasia and inflammation.
source: Regulation of necroptotic signaling is crucial for skin homeostasis because deletion of either caspase-8, the caspase-8 adaptor protein FADD (Fas-associated protein with death domain), or RIPK1, leads to RIPK3- and MLKL-dependent epidermal hyperplasia and inflammation (Kovalenko et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2009; Bonnet et al., 2011; Kaiser et al., 2011; Oberst et al., 2011; Dannappel et al., 2014; Dillon et al., 2014; Rickard et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: High levels of RIPK3, loss of cIAPs, and CYLD-mediated deubiquitylation of RIPK1 appear conducive to necroptosis.
source: Although the precise factors that determine whether TNFR1 mediates apoptosis or necroptosis are unclear, high levels of RIPK3, loss of cIAPs, and CYLD-mediated deubiquitylation of RIPK1 appear conducive to necroptosis (Silke and Vaux, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: RIPK3 may regulate inflammasome-induced IL-1β production in the absence of IAPs or caspase-8.
source: In addition to a crucial role in necroptosis, RIPK3 may also regulate inflammasome-induced IL-1ß production in the absence of IAPs or caspase-8 (Vince et al., 2012; Kang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: MLKL is downstream of RIPK3 in necroptosis and appears not to be required for cytokine production in the same situations as RIPK3.
source: MLKL is downstream of RIPK3 in necroptosis and appears not to be required for cytokine production in the same situations as RIPK3 (Wong et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Shpnm/mTnfr1−/− mice showed no outward signs of disease even after 35 weeks.
source: Tnfr2 deletion did not ameliorate the dermatitis but Shpnm/mTnfr1−/− mice showed no outward signs of disease even after 35 weeks (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Il1r1 deletion significantly delayed the appearance of dermatitis in Shpnm/m mice.
source: Il1r1 deletion significantly delayed the appearance of dermatitis, with markedly reduced epidermal hyperplasia in 13-week-old Shpnm/mIl1r1−/− mice compared with 12-week-old Shpnm/m mice (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: By 19–20 weeks, Shpnm/mIl1r1−/− mice typically developed disease and required euthanasia.
source: However, by 19–20 weeks, Shpnm/mIl1r1−/− mice typically developed disease and required euthanasia.
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: Tnfr1 deletion reduced periportal liver inflammation and partially ameliorated the splenic phenotype in Shpnm/m mice.
source: Tnfr1 deletion reduced periportal liver inflammation and partially ameliorated the splenic phenotype, but did not restore Peyer's patches, whilst Tnfr2 and Il1r1 deletion did not prevent pathology in any of these organs (Figure 1B,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Tnfr1 deletion did not restore Peyer's patches in Shpnm/m mice.
source: Tnfr1 deletion reduced periportal liver inflammation and partially ameliorated the splenic phenotype, but did not restore Peyer's patches, whilst Tnfr2 and Il1r1 deletion did not prevent pathology in any of these organs (Figure 1B,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Tnfr2 and Il1r1 deletion did not prevent liver, spleen, or intestinal pathology in Shpnm/m mice.
source: Tnfr1 deletion reduced periportal liver inflammation and partially ameliorated the splenic phenotype, but did not restore Peyer's patches, whilst Tnfr2 and Il1r1 deletion did not prevent pathology in any of these organs (Figure 1B,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: TNF levels were slightly elevated in 6-week-old cpdm skin.
source: TNF levels were slightly elevated (log scale, Figure 2A)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: IL-5 was elevated in 6-week-old cpdm skin.
source: and, consistent with reports of eosinophilia in cpdm mice (HogenEsch et al., 1993; Gijbels et al., 1996), IL-5 (a key inducer of eosinophil maturation) was also elevated.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2A, with supporting citations.

claim: MCP-1 was significantly elevated in 6-week-old cpdm skin.
source: The monocyte and macrophage chemoattractant protein MCP-1 was significantly elevated in cpdm skin, as was the IL-12 p40 subunit.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: IL-12 p40 subunit was significantly elevated in 6-week-old cpdm skin.
source: The monocyte and macrophage chemoattractant protein MCP-1 was significantly elevated in cpdm skin, as was the IL-12 p40 subunit.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: There was a trend for MIP-1α levels to be elevated in 6-week-old cpdm skin.
source: There was also a trend for macrophage inflammatory protein 1α (MIP-1α) levels to be elevated.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: There was an increase in F4/80+ cells in the Shpnm/m dermis at 3 weeks, before significant epidermal hyperplasia was present.
source: Consistent with this, there was an increase in F4/80+ cells in the Shpnm/m dermis, and this was evident in patches at 3 weeks, before significant epidermal hyperplasia was present (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Cleaved caspase-3-positive cells were present in the epidermis of 3-week-old Shpnm/m mice.
source: Ikeda et al. reported cleaved caspase-3-positive keratinocytes in 10-week-old Shpnm/m mice (Ikeda et al., 2011), and we found cleaved caspase-3-positive cells were already present in the epidermis of 3-week-old Shpnm/m mice, indicating that apoptosis is an early event in the dermatitis and occurs before significant hyperplasia (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2C, with a supporting citation.

claim: Apoptosis is an early event in cpdm dermatitis and occurs before significant hyperplasia.
source: Ikeda et al. reported cleaved caspase-3-positive keratinocytes in 10-week-old Shpnm/m mice (Ikeda et al., 2011), and we found cleaved caspase-3-positive cells were already present in the epidermis of 3-week-old Shpnm/m mice, indicating that apoptosis is an early event in the dermatitis and occurs before significant hyperplasia (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of cleaved caspase-3-positive cells at 3 weeks before significant hyperplasia.

claim: There were slightly more cleaved caspase-3-positive cells in Shpnm/m livers than controls, almost exclusively in the infiltrating cells.
source: There were slightly more cleaved caspase-3-positive cells in Shpnm/m livers than controls (almost exclusively in the infiltrating cells), however they were infrequent.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: An increased number of cleaved caspase-3-positive cells were detected in Shpnm/m spleens, but were much less appreciable than in the epidermis.
source: An increased number of cleaved caspase-3-positive cells were detected in Shpnm/m spleens, but, again, were much less appreciable than in the epidermis (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Wild-type mice reconstituted with Shpnm/m bone marrow cells did not demonstrate any skin, liver, or spleen phenotype during 12 months of observation.
source: To test this possibility, we reconstituted wild-type mice with Shpnm/m bone marrow cells and followed them for 12 months. Reconstitution efficiency was high but the mice did not demonstrate any skin, liver, or spleen phenotype during this time (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The hematopoietic system in isolation cannot cause Shpnm/m dermatitis.
source: Collectively these results suggest that the hematopoietic system in isolation cannot cause Shpnm/m dermatitis, and that macrophages may play a role in the amplification of the disease, particularly given they can be a prominent source of TNF.
evidence: This is inferred from the bone marrow reconstitution experiments showing no disease transfer.

claim: Macrophages may play a role in the amplification of Shpnm/m dermatitis.
source: Collectively these results suggest that the hematopoietic system in isolation cannot cause Shpnm/m dermatitis, and that macrophages may play a role in the amplification of the disease, particularly given they can be a prominent source of TNF.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation of macrophage infiltration and their potential as a TNF source.

claim: TNF-induced cell death in Shpnm/m keratinocytes was partially blocked by Q-VD-OPh or Nec-1 treatment.
source: Consistent with this, TNF-induced cell death in Shpnm/m keratinocytes that was partially blocked by Q-VD-OPh or Nec-1 treatment (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Shpnm/m mouse dermal fibroblasts were sensitive to TNF-induced cell death.
source: Shpnm/m mouse dermal fibroblasts (MDFs) were also sensitive to TNF-induced cell death, and this death was almost completely blocked by the RIPK1 kinase inhibitor Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1), but not by the pan-caspase inhibitor Q-VD-OPh (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: TNF-induced cell death in Shpnm/m mouse dermal fibroblasts was almost completely blocked by Nec-1, but not by Q-VD-OPh.
source: Shpnm/m mouse dermal fibroblasts (MDFs) were also sensitive to TNF-induced cell death, and this death was almost completely blocked by the RIPK1 kinase inhibitor Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1), but not by the pan-caspase inhibitor Q-VD-OPh (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: TNF treatment led to caspase-3 and -8 cleavage at 4 hr in Shpnm/m, but not wild-type, keratinocytes.
source: TNF treatment led to caspase-3 and -8 cleavage at 4 hr in Shpnm/m, but not wild-type, keratinocytes.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: In Shpnm/m MDFs there was caspase-3 and -8 cleavage, and this was reduced by Nec-1, but not Q-VD, treatment.
source: In Shpnm/m MDFs there was also caspase-3 and -8 cleavage, and, surprisingly, this was reduced by Nec-1, but not Q-VD, treatment (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: In Shpnm/m keratinocytes and MDFs, the increased caspase-8 activity coincided with a marked processing of cFLIP.
source: In Shpnm/m keratinocytes and MDFs, the increased caspase-8 activity coincided with a marked processing of cFLIP, but other outcomes of the signaling pathway were less obviously affected.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: TNF-induced apoptosis may play a pathogenic role in the Shpnm/m skin phenotype.
source: Together with the early presence of cleaved caspase-3 staining and the elevation of TNF in Shpnm/m skin, these results indicate that TNF-induced apoptosis may play a pathogenic role in the skin phenotype.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined observations of cleaved caspase-3 staining, elevated TNF, and caspase cleavage in response to TNF.

claim: Shpnm/m neutrophils, monocytes and bone-marrow-derived macrophages were all sensitive to killing by TNF, whereas wild-type cells were not.
source: Shpnm/m neutrophils, monocytes and bone-marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) were all sensitive to killing by TNF, whereas the wild-type cells were not (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Neutrophil and monocyte cell death was more efficiently blocked by a combination of Nec-1 and Q-VD.
source: Neutrophil and monocyte cell death was more efficiently blocked by a combination of Nec-1 and Q-VD, whereas in macrophages Nec-1 was sufficient to block cell death.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: In Shpnm/m macrophages, Nec-1 was sufficient to block TNF-induced cell death.
source: Neutrophil and monocyte cell death was more efficiently blocked by a combination of Nec-1 and Q-VD, whereas in macrophages Nec-1 was sufficient to block cell death.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Myeloid cell death may contribute to the inflammatory skin phenotype in Shpnm/m mice.
source: These data suggest that myeloid cell death may contribute to the inflammatory skin phenotype.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation that myeloid cells are sensitive to TNF-induced death.

claim: Substantially reduced linear ubiquitylation was detected in the native TNFR1 signaling complex obtained from Shpnm/m vs wild-type MEFs.
source: Consistent with earlier reports (Gerlach et al., 2011; Peltzer et al., 2014), however, using an antibody that specifically recognises linear ubiquitin we detected substantially reduced linear ubiquitylation in the native TNFR1 signaling complex obtained from Shpnm/m vs wild-type mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 5A, with supporting citations.

claim: HaCaT keratinocytes stably expressing catalytically inactive HOIPC885S were sensitive to TNF-induced cell death.
source: We also found that HaCaT keratinocytes (a human immortalized cell line) stably expressing catalytically inactive HOIPC885S were sensitive to TNF-induced cell death (Figure 5B), indicating a requirement for LUBAC and its linear-ubiquitin-chain-forming activity in preventing TNF-induced keratinocyte death.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: LUBAC and its linear-ubiquitin-chain-forming activity are required for preventing TNF-induced keratinocyte death.
source: We also found that HaCaT keratinocytes (a human immortalized cell line) stably expressing catalytically inactive HOIPC885S were sensitive to TNF-induced cell death (Figure 5B), indicating a requirement for LUBAC and its linear-ubiquitin-chain-forming activity in preventing TNF-induced keratinocyte death.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that catalytically inactive HOIP sensitizes keratinocytes to TNF-induced death.

claim: 12-week-old Shpnm/mCasp8+/− mice had almost no epidermal hyperplasia and largely normal keratin 6 and 14 expression.
source: In contrast to Shpnm/m mice, 12-week-old Shpnm/mCasp8+/− mice had almost no epidermal hyperplasia and largely normal keratin 6 and 14 expression (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: By 15 weeks of age, significant hyperplasia was observed in one Shpnm/mCasp8+/− mouse.
source: By 15 weeks of age, however, significant hyperplasia was observed in one of these mice (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Shpnm/mCasp8+/− mice retained splenomegaly with disrupted splenic architecture, liver inflammation, and a lack of intestinal Peyer's patches.
source: Shpnm/mCasp8+/− mice retained other aspects of the phenotype: splenomegaly with disrupted splenic architecture, liver inflammation, and a lack of intestinal Peyer's patches (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Shpnm/mBid−/− mice showed no protection from any aspects of the cpdm phenotype.
source: We observed no protection from any aspects of the cpdm phenotype (Figure 6A–D), however, indicating that caspase-8, but not BID, is an important driver of this disease.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 6A-D.

claim: Caspase-8, but not BID, is an important driver of cpdm disease.
source: We observed no protection from any aspects of the cpdm phenotype (Figure 6A–D), however, indicating that caspase-8, but not BID, is an important driver of this disease.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Casp8 heterozygosity delays dermatitis while Bid deletion does not protect.

claim: Roughly half of 12-week-old Shpnm/mRipk3−/− mice had a less severe epidermal phenotype compared to control mice.
source: Whereas control mice invariably developed severe dermatitis by 12 weeks of age, roughly half of the 12-week-old Shpnm/mRipk3−/− mice had a less severe epidermal phenotype at this point (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: All Shpnm/mRipk3−/− animals aged over 12 weeks went on to develop severe disease and were euthanized due to their skin phenotype before 18 weeks of age.
source: When aged over 12 weeks, all Shpnm/mRipk3−/− animals went on to develop severe disease and were euthanized due to their skin phenotype before 18 weeks of age.
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: 12-week-old Shpnm/mRipk3−/− mice had no signs of liver inflammation and significantly less splenomegaly.
source: 12 week-old Shpnm/mRipk3−/− mice had no signs of liver inflammation and significantly less splenomegaly, although they still lacked Peyer's patches (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: 12-week-old Shpnm/mRipk3−/− mice still lacked Peyer's patches.
source: 12 week-old Shpnm/mRipk3−/− mice had no signs of liver inflammation and significantly less splenomegaly, although they still lacked Peyer's patches (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: Shpnm/mMlkl−/− mice had a similar epidermal phenotype to Shpnm/m mice.
source: We also generated Shpnm/mMlkl−/− mice and found they had a similar epidermal phenotype to Shpnm/m mice (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: 12-week-old Shpnm/mMlkl−/− mice had reduced splenomegaly and only one out of 12 mice showed signs of liver inflammation.
source: Like Shpnm/mRipk3−/− mice, however, 12-week-old Shpnm/mMlkl−/− animals had reduced splenomegaly and only one out of 12 mice showed signs of liver inflammation (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: RIPK3 and MLKL are important drivers of the liver and splenic cpdm phenotype.
source: Collectively these results indicate that RIPK3 and MLKL are important drivers of the liver and splenic cpdm phenotype, and that RIPK3 contributes to the epidermal phenotype, importantly in a non-MLKL-dependent (hence, most likely, necroptosis-independent) manner.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ripk3 and Mlkl deletion ameliorate liver and spleen phenotypes.

claim: RIPK3 contributes to the epidermal phenotype in a non-MLKL-dependent (hence, most likely, necroptosis-independent) manner.
source: Collectively these results indicate that RIPK3 and MLKL are important drivers of the liver and splenic cpdm phenotype, and that RIPK3 contributes to the epidermal phenotype, importantly in a non-MLKL-dependent (hence, most likely, necroptosis-independent) manner.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ripk3 deletion delays dermatitis while Mlkl deletion does not.

claim: Most Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− mice died perinatally, typically in a window between E17 and 1 to 2 days after birth.
source: At one facility, most of these triple-deficient mice died perinatally, typically in a window between E17 and 1 to 2 days after birth, and no Shpnm/mCasp8-/-Ripk3−/− animals were obtained at weaning (Figure 8A,B; numbers in A refer to mice analyzed at first facility only).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 8A,B.

claim: No Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− animals were obtained at weaning at one facility.
source: At one facility, most of these triple-deficient mice died perinatally, typically in a window between E17 and 1 to 2 days after birth, and no Shpnm/mCasp8-/-Ripk3−/− animals were obtained at weaning (Figure 8A,B; numbers in A refer to mice analyzed at first facility only).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Most Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− embryos obtained by Caesarean section at E19 appeared edematous or were dead.
source: Most Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− embryos obtained by Caesarean section at E19 appeared edematous or were dead.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Two viable Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− mice were obtained from a limited number of matings at a separate facility.
source: At a separate facility, two viable Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− mice were obtained from a limited number of matings.
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: The two viable Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− mice appeared runted by roughly 3 months of age and were euthanized.
source: By roughly 3 months of age these mice appeared runted and were euthanized.
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: The two viable Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− mice had no epidermal phenotype, but disrupted splenic architecture was apparent.
source: Histologically these mice had no epidermal phenotype, but disrupted splenic architecture was apparent (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Shpnm/mCasp8+/−Ripk3−/− mice were indistinguishable from control mice at 12 weeks of age and had no skin, liver, or spleen pathology.
source: These mice were indistinguishable from control mice at 12 weeks of age and had no skin, liver, or spleen pathology (Figure 9A–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 9A-E.

claim: Peyer's patches were present in Shpnm/mCasp8+/−Ripk3−/− mice.
source: Remarkably, Peyer's patches were present (Figure 9C, Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 9C and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: One 67-week-old and three 45-week-old Shpnm/mCasp8+/−Ripk3−/− mice had no signs of any skin phenotype.
source: One 67-week-old and three 45-week-old Shpnm/mCasp8+/−Ripk3−/− mice had no signs of any skin phenotype, however another mouse developed dermatitis at 42 weeks (Figure 9A,B,D; note that epidermal thickness was not quantified for the 42-week-old mouse).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 9A,B,D.

claim: One Shpnm/mCasp8+/−Ripk3−/− mouse developed dermatitis at 42 weeks.
source: One 67-week-old and three 45-week-old Shpnm/mCasp8+/−Ripk3−/− mice had no signs of any skin phenotype, however another mouse developed dermatitis at 42 weeks (Figure 9A,B,D; note that epidermal thickness was not quantified for the 42-week-old mouse).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 9A,B,D.

claim: Tnfr1 deletion was more effective at reducing leukocyte numbers than Tnfr2 or Il1r1 deletion.
source: Tnfr1 deletion was more effective at reducing leukocyte numbers than Tnfr2 or Il1r1 deletion, although all of these compound knock-out mice had leukocyte subsets that were elevated compared to controls.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 10.

claim: Caspase-8 heterozygosity or Bid deletion did not prevent the leukocytosis in Shpnm/m mice.
source: Caspase-8 heterozygosity or Bid deletion did not prevent the leukocytosis, whereas Ripk3 and Mlkl deletion markedly reduced it, suggesting the hematopoietic phenotype is driven predominantly by necroptosis.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 10.

claim: Ripk3 and Mlkl deletion markedly reduced leukocytosis in Shpnm/m mice.
source: Caspase-8 heterozygosity or Bid deletion did not prevent the leukocytosis, whereas Ripk3 and Mlkl deletion markedly reduced it, suggesting the hematopoietic phenotype is driven predominantly by necroptosis.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 10.

claim: The hematopoietic phenotype in Shpnm/m mice is driven predominantly by necroptosis.
source: Caspase-8 heterozygosity or Bid deletion did not prevent the leukocytosis, whereas Ripk3 and Mlkl deletion markedly reduced it, suggesting the hematopoietic phenotype is driven predominantly by necroptosis.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ripk3 and Mlkl deletion markedly reduce leukocytosis.

claim: Shpnm/mRipk3−/− and Shpnm/mMlkl−/− mice still had elevated neutrophils.
source: Shpnm/mRipk3−/− and Shpnm/mMlkl−/− mice still had elevated neutrophils, however Shpnm/mCasp8+/−Ripk3−/− mice had no white blood cell elevation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 10.

claim: Shpnm/mCasp8+/−Ripk3−/− mice had no white blood cell elevation.
source: Shpnm/mRipk3−/− and Shpnm/mMlkl−/− mice still had elevated neutrophils, however Shpnm/mCasp8+/−Ripk3−/− mice had no white blood cell elevation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 10.

claim: Loss of HOIP causes mid-gestational embryonic lethality (embryonic day 10.5), and this is prevented by simultaneous loss of Tnfr1.
source: Lack of HOIP causes mid-gestational embryonic lethality (embryonic day 10.5), and this is prevented by simultaneous loss of Tnfr1 (Peltzer et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: LUBAC is required for full-strength IL-1β and TNF signaling.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that LUBAC is required for full-strength IL-1ß and TNF signaling and deficiency in these signaling pathways would be expected to impair an inflammatory response.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on cited evidence.

claim: Loss-of-expression and loss-of-function mutations in HOIL-1 result in a fatal, human, inherited disorder characterized by chronic inflammation.
source: Likewise, loss-of-expression and loss-of-function mutations in HOIL-1 result in a fatal, human, inherited disorder characterized by chronic inflammation; consistent with loss of the major defensive inflammatory signaling pathways, affected patients suffer from invasive bacterial infections (Boisson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Patients with HOIL-1 mutations suffer from invasive bacterial infections.
source: Likewise, loss-of-expression and loss-of-function mutations in HOIL-1 result in a fatal, human, inherited disorder characterized by chronic inflammation; consistent with loss of the major defensive inflammatory signaling pathways, affected patients suffer from invasive bacterial infections (Boisson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: The inflammatory skin phenotype in Shpnm/m mutant mice is the result of an intrinsic skin defect.
source: The work described here excludes this caveat because reconstituted mice did not develop signs of the cpdm phenotype even a year after reconstitution; thus, the inflammatory skin phenotype in the Shpnm/m mutant mice is the result of an intrinsic skin defect.
evidence: This is inferred from the bone marrow reconstitution experiments showing no disease transfer over 12 months.

claim: Loss of Mlkl did not affect the Shpnm/m skin phenotype but significantly reduced or prevented splenomegaly and liver inflammation.
source: It is, however, noteworthy that loss of Mlkl did not affect the Shpnm/m skin phenotype but significantly reduced or prevented splenomegaly and liver inflammation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion summarizing the results.

claim: Reduction in caspase-8 markedly ameliorated the skin phenotype but did not prevent splenomegaly or liver inflammation in Shpnm/m mice.
source: Conversely, reduction in caspase-8 markedly ameliorated the skin phenotype but did not prevent splenomegaly or liver inflammation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion summarizing the results.

claim: The skin and systemic phenotype in Shpnm/m mice are separable.
source: This shows that the skin and systemic phenotype are separable, although the exact mechanism is unclear.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of Mlkl and Casp8 deletion on skin vs systemic phenotypes.

claim: Loss of IL-1 signaling suppresses the cpdm phenotype.
source: Loss of IL-1 signaling has been shown to suppress the cpdm phenotype (Liang et al., 2010), but because the environment of the mice likely plays a large part in the onset and severity of the inflammatory disease it was not possible to determine whether loss of IL-1 signaling is as potent as Tnf deficiency at preventing the phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: TNF/TNFR1 signaling is the main driver of inflammation in cpdm mice and IL-1 contributes to exacerbating the disease.
source: These data are again consistent with our original hypothesis, suggesting that TNF/TNFR1 signaling is the main driver of inflammation and that IL-1 contributes to exacerbating the disease.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of Tnfr1 and Il1r1 deletion effects on the cpdm phenotype.

claim: Loss of Casp8 or Fadd in the skin leads to keratinocyte hyperplasia and inflammatory skin disease.
source: Casp8 deficiency results in early embryonic lethality in mice (Varfolomeev et al., 1998), and loss of Casp8 or Fadd in the skin leads to keratinocyte hyperplasia and inflammatory skin disease (Kovalenko et al., 2009; Bonnet et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: The intrinsic mitochondrial pathway is unlikely to play a significant role in cpdm disease.
source: Genetic deletion of Bid did not suppress the dermatitis or any other aspect of the cpdm phenotype, therefore we conclude that the intrinsic mitochondrial pathway is unlikely to play a significant role in the disease.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Bid deletion does not protect against the cpdm phenotype.

claim: Apoptosis is the main driver of Shpnm/m dermatitis.
source: Combined with the markedly ameliorated dermatitis seen in Shpnm/mCasp8+/− mice, this indicates that apoptosis is the main driver of Shpnm/m dermatitis.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Casp8 heterozygosity delays dermatitis while Mlkl deletion does not.

claim: When in excess, apoptosis can result in severe inflammation.
source: Although apoptosis is generally regarded as being immunologically inert, when in excess it can result in severe inflammation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as general knowledge.

claim: Conditional deletion of cFLIP in adult keratinocytes caused severe inflammation in the epidermis.
source: For example, conditional deletion of cFLIP in adult keratinocytes caused severe inflammation in the epidermis (Panayotova-Dimitrova et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: The inflammation caused by conditional deletion of cFLIP in adult keratinocytes was TNF dependent.
source: Like the cpdm phenotype, this inflammation was TNF dependent.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with reference to cited work.

claim: An excess of apoptotic cells may cause disease by overwhelming phagocytosis and clearance of apoptotic bodies, leading to secondary necrosis and DAMP release.
source: An excess of apoptotic cells may cause disease by overwhelming phagocytosis and clearance of apoptotic bodies, leading to secondary necrosis and DAMP release.
evidence: This is speculated as a potential mechanism for how excessive apoptosis causes inflammation.

claim: In certain contexts, such as viral infections, apoptosis may be inflammatory.
source: It has also been proposed that in certain contexts, such as viral infections, apoptosis may be inflammatory (Cullen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Sharpin deficiency triggers apoptosis in some tissues but necroptosis in others.
source: In other Shpnm/m organs such as the liver, spleen, and hematopoietic system, Ripk3 and Mlkl deletion ameliorated or protected against disease, indicating that Sharpin deficiency triggers apoptosis in some tissues but necroptosis in others.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of Ripk3/Mlkl deletion on different organs.

claim: The post-natal regression of Peyer's patches in Shpnm/m mice is due to deregulated cell death.
source: Our data show that whilst neither Casp8 heterozygosity nor Ripk3 deletion in isolation restored intestinal Peyer's patches, the combination was able to do so. This suggests that the post-natal regression of these secondary lymphoid organs in Shpnm/m mice is due to deregulated cell death.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that combined Casp8 heterozygosity and Ripk3 deletion restores Peyer's patches.

claim: Crossing cpdm mice with Ripk1K45A/K45A mice (which lack RIPK1 kinase activity) completely suppresses the cpdm phenotype.
source: In a wider sense, our results are particularly important when interpreting the recent finding that crossing cpdm mice with Ripk1K45A/K45A mice (which lack RIPK1 kinase activity) completely suppresses the cpdm phenotype (Berger et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: In the context of the Shpnm/m epidermis, the dominant role of the RIPK1 kinase domain is to activate apoptosis.
source: Taken together with the work of Berger et al. our work inescapably suggests that in the context of the Shpnm/m epidermis the dominant role of the RIPK1 kinase domain is to activate apoptosis.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined observations that the skin phenotype is driven by apoptosis and that RIPK1 kinase activity is required for the phenotype.

claim: Nec-1 blocked TNF-induced caspase-8 and caspase-3 activation in Shpnm/m dermal fibroblasts.
source: Unexpectedly, but supporting this conclusion, we showed that Nec-1 (the RIPK1 kinase inhibitor) blocked TNF-induced caspase-8 and caspase-3 activation in Shpnm/m dermal fibroblasts.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion summarizing the results shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Loss of RIPK1 in the skin results in a RIPK3/MLKL-dependent hyperplasia that is presumably dependent on necroptosis.
source: This conclusion is particularly confronting because we and others have shown that loss of RIPK1 in the skin results in a RIPK3/MLKL-dependent hyperplasia that is presumably dependent on necroptosis (Dannappel et al., 2014; Rickard et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: RIPK1 is able to both activate and inhibit either apoptosis or necroptosis in a highly context-dependent manner.
source: Thus RIPK1 is able to both activate and inhibit either apoptosis or necroptosis in a highly context-dependent manner.
evidence: This is inferred from the apparently contradictory roles of RIPK1 in different contexts.

claim: Ripk3 deletion prevents the embryonic lethality seen with either Fadd or Casp8 deletion and the mice survive to adulthood.
source: Ripk3 deletion prevents the embryonic lethality seen with either Fadd or Casp8 deletion and the mice survive to adulthood (Kaiser et al., 2011; Oberst et al., 2011; Dillon et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: The perinatal lethality observed in Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− mice was completely unexpected.
source: Given this, the perinatal lethality we observed in Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− mice was completely unexpected.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion expressing surprise at the finding.

claim: Environmental differences contribute to the variable penetrance of the Shpnm/mCasp8−/−Ripk3−/− phenotype.
source: Exon 3- and 4-deleted caspase-8 mice in yet a third facility (not shown), however, did not survive past weaning, indicating that environmental differences undoubtedly also contribute to the variable penetrance.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of different outcomes at different facilities.

claim: TNFR1-induced cell death is a driver of the inflammatory disease in cpdm mice.
source: In summary, we provide strong evidence that Sharpin deficiency sensitizes keratinocytes to TNF/TNFR1-induced, caspase-8-mediated apoptosis, and that this defect appears to drive the cpdm dermatitis.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary conclusion.

claim: Sharpin deficiency sensitizes keratinocytes to TNF/TNFR1-induced, caspase-8-mediated apoptosis.
source: In summary, we provide strong evidence that Sharpin deficiency sensitizes keratinocytes to TNF/TNFR1-induced, caspase-8-mediated apoptosis, and that this defect appears to drive the cpdm dermatitis.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary conclusion.

claim: Only combined Casp8 heterozygosity and Ripk3 deficiency was able to almost completely prevent all aspects of the cpdm systemic phenotype, including the early loss of Peyer's patches.
source: Only combined Casp8 heterozygosity and Ripk3 deficiency was able to almost completely prevent all aspects of the cpdm systemic phenotype that we evaluated, including the early loss of Peyer's patches.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary conclusion.

claim: Excessive apoptosis can cause inflammatory disease.
source: Whilst inflammation is a known sequelae to necroptotic DAMP release, these findings provide further evidence that excessive apoptosis can also cause inflammatory disease.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the findings.

claim: The suppression of cpdm dermatitis seen by crossing to mice lacking RIPK1 kinase activity may be due to RIPK1's kinase activity being upstream of caspase-8 in mediating TNF-induced apoptosis.
source: Furthermore, these results indicate that the suppression of cpdm dermatitis seen by crossing to mice lacking RIPK1 kinase activity (Berger et al., 2014) may, surprisingly, be due to RIPK1's kinase activity being upstream of caspase-8 in mediating TNF-induced apoptosis.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the findings, with a supporting citation.

claim: Rudimentary Peyer's patches formed in Shpnm/m embryos, but these regressed post-natally.
source: A recent study, however, demonstrated that rudimentary Peyer's patches formed in Shpnm/m embryos, but that these regressed post-natally (Seymour et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.
